{
  "hazard_consequence_node": [
    {
      "label": "HazardConsequence",
      "name": "BLEVE",
      "node_id": "H1",
      "node_type": "HazardConsequence",
      "evidence": "The Executive Summary states that 'the pressure vessel failure caused a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE).' Section 2.1.2 further concludes that 'the catastrophic failure of the SCR meets the definition of a BLEVE' because pressurized water above its atmospheric boiling point was suddenly released, causing rapid boiling, blast effects, and vessel rocketing.",
      "explanation": "The incident analysis is centered on catastrophic rupture of the Semi-Closed Receiver containing hot pressurized water, followed by sudden flashing and vapor expansion. The report explicitly names this mechanism as a BLEVE and analyzes corrosion, thinning, rupture, and rapid depressurization as the main accident phenomenon.",
      "source": "Not specified"
    }
  ],
  "entity_nodes": [
    {
      "label": "Material",
      "name": "Water",
      "node_id": "En1",
      "node_type": "Entity",
      "evidence": "The SCR typically contained water held at around 100 psig and 330℉",
      "explanation": "Hot pressurized water in the SCR was the material that suddenly depressurized, flashed, and produced the BLEVE.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Location",
      "name": "Semi-Closed Receiver (SCR)",
      "node_id": "En2",
      "node_type": "Entity",
      "evidence": "the bottom head of a pressure vessel called a Semi-Closed Receiver",
      "explanation": "The failed equipment was the Semi-Closed Receiver pressure vessel in Loy-Lange's steam system.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Location",
      "name": "Loy-Lange Box Company, St. Louis, Missouri",
      "node_id": "En3",
      "node_type": "Entity",
      "evidence": "an explosion occurred at the Loy-Lange Box Company (Loy-Lange) in St. Louis, Missouri.",
      "explanation": "The incident occurred at the Loy-Lange facility in St. Louis, Missouri.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ],
  "condition_nodes": [
    {
      "label": "Phase",
      "name": "Liquid",
      "node_id": "C1",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "the water in the SCR was contained at a temperature greater than its atmospheric boiling point and at a pressure sufficiently high to suppress boiling.",
      "explanation": "Before rupture, the hazardous material was contained as liquid water under pressure; it flashed after the vessel failed.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Pressure",
      "name": "High pressure",
      "node_id": "C2",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "The SCR typically contained water held at around 100 psig",
      "explanation": "The water was stored under elevated pressure in the SCR, enabling rapid depressurization on failure.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Temperature",
      "name": "High temperature",
      "node_id": "C3",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "The SCR typically contained water held at around 100 psig and 330℉",
      "explanation": "The water temperature was above its atmospheric boiling point, so sudden pressure loss caused flashing and vapor expansion.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "ReleaseType",
      "name": "Instant release",
      "node_id": "C4",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "resulted in a sudden loss of containment",
      "explanation": "The bottom head rupture abruptly released the vessel contents and caused immediate depressurization.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Confinement",
      "name": "High confinement",
      "node_id": "C5",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "containment that causes the pressure on the liquid to be sufficiently high to suppress boiling",
      "explanation": "The water was enclosed within a pressure vessel, providing the confinement needed to maintain it as hot pressurized liquid until rupture.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ],
  "event_nodes": [
    {
      "label": "InitiatingEvent",
      "name": "Leak from underneath the SCR",
      "node_id": "Ev1",
      "node_type": "Event",
      "evidence": "observed a leak that appeared to be coming from underneath the SCR.",
      "explanation": "The leak was the first abnormal event immediately preceding the final failure sequence and indicated loss of vessel integrity before continued operation and restart.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "MechanicalFailure",
      "name": "Catastrophic failure of the SCR bottom head",
      "node_id": "Ev2",
      "node_type": "Event",
      "evidence": "the SCR bottom head catastrophically failed.",
      "explanation": "The corroded and thinned bottom head ruptured, causing sudden loss of containment and initiating the BLEVE.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ]
}
